xml.name: Kyero XML
xml.description: The Kyero-format feed (version 3) exported by Casafari, Estatebud and most CRMs, by URL or file.

tivvu.name: My own system (Tivvu XML)
tivvu.description: If your system has its own API, generate the Tivvu XML and we read that feed by URL or file.

shared.tableTips: If you can, include: a unique reference column (ID) per property (so re-importing updates instead of duplicating), title, type, listing type, price, location, description and photos (links).
shared.review: Check the preview: nothing is saved until you confirm.
shared.provideTable: Paste the file's URL (CSV or Excel) in the box alongside, or upload the file. We suggest the column mapping automatically.
shared.provideFeed: Paste the feed URL in the box alongside, or upload the XML.

help.body: I want to move my properties from {origin} to Tivvu and I don't know how to get the data or how to import it. Can you help me?

steps.s1: Casafari offers a property feed by URL (in Kyero, XML2U or ACME-CRM format) that updates every 20 minutes, but their support team turns it on: ask them with the button below (help@casafaricrm.com) and choose the Kyero format.
steps.s2: In the Kyero export, properties without price, district, city or type are left out: fill them in first.

casafari-crm.note: Casafari's Properties › Export › Portals Catalogue menu is for publishing on portals like Kyero, not for getting your feed.

sources.s1: Casafari help: integration with external systems

steps.s1: Go to c.estatebud.com, open Admin › Plugins, install the Kyero plugin and confirm the installation.
steps.s2: In Admin › Plugins › Kyero copy the “XML Feed URL”.
steps.s3: Mark which properties go into the feed: on each one, Actions Menu › Listings › Kyero › Save; or in bulk, select several and use Bulk Edit › “Add listings on” › Kyero. If a required field is missing, Estatebud tells you which.

estatebud.note: These steps come from a guide by INDEX.cy (a portal), not from Estatebud's help: if a menu has changed, ask their support.

steps.s1: Kyero doesn't hand out your feed: it receives it from your CRM. Ask your CRM or provider for the Kyero feed URL (XML version 3) they already send to Kyero.

kyero.note: Each Kyero feed is a full snapshot of a single agency: anything not in the feed is treated as withdrawn.

portal.s1: {name} is a listing portal: your data usually lives in the CRM you publish from, and the most complete option is to move from that CRM (go back and pick it from the list).
portal.s2: If you want to bring over your listings published on {name}, ask their support for the XML feed (ideally in Kyero format): the message is ready below.

aggregator.s1: {name} aggregates and converts feeds from other systems: the most complete option is to move from the CRM that sends it the data (go back and pick it from the list).
aggregator.s2: If you have an XML feed from {name} (ideally in Kyero format), use it; if not, ask their support with the message below.

crm.s1: Get the XML feed of your properties from {name}, ideally in Kyero format (version 3). If you don't know where it is, ask their support: the message below is ready to send.

ownSteps.s1: Generate an XML in Tivvu format from your API (example below): one '<listing>' per property.
ownSteps.s2: Always use the same '<external_id>' for the same property, so re-importing updates instead of duplicating.
ownSteps.s3: Publish the XML at a public URL and paste it in the box alongside, or upload the file.

kyeroSteps.s1: Get the XML feed of your properties in Kyero format (version 3) from your CRM: most CRMs generate it to publish on portals.

tableSteps.s1: Get your properties in a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file. If you're starting from scratch, download the template below.

routeSteps.kyero: If {name} can give you a Kyero-format feed (XML), copy its public URL or download the file.
routeSteps.table: Get your properties from {name} in a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file.

mapping.noReference: Without a reference column (ID), re-importing the file will duplicate the properties instead of updating them.
